page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.26xlarge is a high-density, compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8269CY processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 104 dedicated virtual CPU cores alongside 192.0 GB of system memory. This architecture establishes a compute-focused ratio of approximately 1.85 GB of RAM per vCPU, targeted at applications with intense compute requirements relative to memory capacity.

Network connectivity features a baseline throughput of 25 Gbps, supporting stable communication for distributed systems and multi-node clusters. The instance comes with no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached block storage volumes for persistent data retention. It also does not feature hardware GPU acceleration or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying solely on CPU resources and virtual private cloud networking.

With its large core allocation and dedicated compute resources, the ecs.c6.26xlarge delivers substantial compute density per instance. It represents a cost-effective design for workloads that do not demand large per-core memory footprints or expensive local NVMe arrays. Ideal workloads include batch processing pipelines, continuous integration and build systems, distributed data transformation (ETL), scientific modeling, and high-concurrency web serving tiers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.26xlarge is a compute-optimized cloud instance designed for high-concurrency, processor-intensive workloads. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, it features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz with 104 dedicated vCPUs. The server is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, offering an allocation of roughly 1.85 GB of memory per core. The instance provides 25 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth to accommodate demanding multi-node data transfers. No local physical storage is bundled with the instance, necessitating external block storage for operating system and application storage needs. Without hardware GPUs, the platform prioritizes pure multi-core x86 compute efficiency over acceleration. The ecs.c6.26xlarge is structurally suited for scalable backend tasks, batch data processing, software compilation clusters, and compute-focused microservice architectures.
